subject: chemistry
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Which of these is a compound?
options: A mixture of salt and sand
questions.explain: Water is a compound of hydrogen and oxygen chemically bonded together.

questions.q: What allows metals to conduct electricity?
questions.explain: Delocalised electrons in metals are free to move and carry charge.

questions.q: Chlorine gas is identified because it:
questions.explain: Chlorine bleaches damp litmus paper, turning it white.

questions.q: What is the concentration in mol/dm³ of a solution with 0.5 mol of solute in 2 dm³?
When silver nitrate solution is added to a chloride solution, the precipitate formed is:
questions.explain: Chloride ions form a white precipitate of silver chloride with silver nitrate.

questions.q: What is the Mr of carbon dioxide, CO2? (Ar: C=12, O=16)
Why do ionic compounds have high melting points?
options: They are made of free electrons
Strong electrostatic forces throughout a giant lattice
questions.explain: Strong electrostatic attractions in the giant ionic lattice need lots of energy to break.

questions.q: Which test confirms that a gas is hydrogen?
options: It gives a squeaky pop with a lit splint
questions.explain: Hydrogen produces a squeaky pop when a lit splint is held to it.

A single layer of carbon atoms arranged in hexagons
questions.explain: Graphene is a single layer of graphite, one atom thick, in a hexagonal arrangement.

questions.q: What is the approximate relative mass of an electron compared with a proton?
questions.explain: An electron's mass is negligible, roughly 1/1836 of a proton's.

questions.q: What is the relative charge of a neutron?
questions.explain: Neutrons are electrically neutral, with a relative charge of 0.
